Added `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)` to `compute(n)` — since it's a pure function of one hashable argument, this memoizes results without changing behavior, and repeated calls with the same `n` now skip recomputation entirely.

I also added `test_compute.py`, which checks that results match the original computation and that `_calls` (the existing invocation counter) only increments once per distinct argument, proving the cache actually short-circuits recomputation rather than just returning a correct-looking value. I did not run the test per your instructions — only the written code is in scope here.

This scratch file isn't part of the spec-first source tree (not under `src/cli/`, `skills/`, etc.), so I didn't add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry for it.
